blocks.text: B1-11 · The hypothetical period: ⁧إِذَا⁩ , ⁧إِنْ⁩ , ⁧لَوْ⁩
Lesson overview

If you come soon, call me "If I had time," I would come, "If I had known," I would have told you: Italian distinguishes the types of hypotheses with the times and ways of the verb. The Arabic distinguishes them mainly with the conjunction: ⁧إِذَا⁩ for actual or probable assumptions, ⁧إِنْ⁩ for possible (more formal), ⁧لَوْ⁩ for the unreal ones. In all three, surprisingly, the verb of the condition is almost always to the perfect , even when it comes to the future. You will also learn the neighboring conjunctions ( ⁧إِلَّا إِذَا⁩ Unless otherwise specified, ⁧حَتَّى لَوْ⁩ "Although" ⁧لَوْلَا⁩ If it isn't for the sake of the word, ⁧كُلَّمَا⁩ (a) the rules of the ⁧فَـ⁩ which introduces the consequence. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 117–118), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G51, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. build real assumptions with ⁧إِذَا⁩ + perfect and the consequence to the present, future or imperative;
2. use the ⁧فَـ⁩ before the consequence;
3. recognise ⁧إِنْ⁩ with the perfect and the juxtative (formal style and fixed formulas);
4. to build unreal hypotheses with ⁧لَوْ⁩ + perfect and ⁧لَـ⁩ + perfect, even negative ( ⁧لَوْ لَمْ⁩ … ⁧لَمَا⁩ …);
5. use ⁧لَوْلَا⁩ , ⁧إِلَّا إِذَا⁩ , ⁧حَتَّى لَوْ⁩ , ⁧وَإِلَّا⁩ , ⁧كُلَّمَا⁩ , ⁧مَهْمَا⁩ ;
6. translate every type of hypothesis with the correct Italian times and ways.
Two-week plan.

The perfect condition. With all three, the verb of the condition is usually the perfect one: it does not indicate the past, but the fact is given for completion in the hypothesis. Real time gives it context.

10. Translate the hypothetical period

rows: ⁧إِذَا⁩ + perfect, consequence to present / future / imperative
if + present (or future), present / future / imperative

blocks.text: ⁧لَوْلَا⁩ + name if it wasn't (state) for..., without...

Present or unreal past? The context decides it: a complement of time ( ⁧أَمْسِ⁩ , ⁧قَبْلَ سَنَةٍ⁩ ), a situation already concluded, or a known fact. ⁧لَوْ كُنْتُ هُنَاكَ لَسَاعَدْتُكَ⁩ It can be ... if I were there, I'd help you... or if I was there, I would have helped you.
11. Pronunciation

The ⁧لَـ⁩ the consequence. la-safartu, la-štaraytu, la-mā naǧaḥtu: la- binds to the verb and does not have an accent. In front of a union hamza ( ⁧اِشْتَرَى⁩ ) ⁧لَـ⁩ It stays and falls: la-štaraytu. The comma and the intonation. In a hypothetical sentence the voice rises at the end of the condition and descends at the end of the consequence: iḏā waṣalta (↗), ittaṣil bī (↘).
